description: A stain is a story that ended at the nearest fire. Almost always.
lore: Fights end. The broken go down where they stand and, some hours on, stand up again beside the nearest tended fire, short a little of whatever they were thinking when it happened. That is the arithmetic of violence here: it costs a thought, not a life. So a stain on the stones is not a marker. It is the start of a story that finished somewhere warmer — an argument gone too far, a robbery on the road, a creature that had to be released the hard way — and by the time the rain gets around to it, the person it came out of has usually walked past it twice without looking down.

Usually. The re-forming needs a tended fire, and the rota has lapsed almost everywhere. Out where the map has gone [[lore/the_quiet|Quiet]], the nearest fire can be a long way to nowhere. The old hands read stains the way trackers read prints: fresh means a scuffle. Faded, far from any light, means don't ask.
gm_notes: Law III's re-forming demonstrated, plus its cold edge: re-forming presupposes a tended fire, and the lapsed rota (Movement IV) makes remote stains genuinely ominous without any villain. 'Don't ask' is deliberate — what happens to the broken with no fire in reach is not written anywhere, and should stay a dread, not a rule.
